trigger: a sink log()/flush() throw (disk full, EMFILE, broken pipe) at the exact moment stderr is itself blocked or backpressured (full pipe to a stalled log collector)
summary: 09e876ba1's own lock-scope-narrowing fix claimed to close the stderr-fallback wedge hazard, but for a sink-throw trigger spdlog invokes the handler synchronously ON the async logger's own single worker thread (verified against vendored spdlog 1.17.0: backend_sink_it_ -> SPDLOG_LOGGER_CATCH -> err_handler_, no thread hop) -- releasing the lock before the I/O does nothing for a thread that IS the one making the blocking call. What was actually closed: cross-thread lock contention (other threads/accessors no longer join the stall via the mutex). What remains open: the worker thread itself still stalls in fprintf/fflush for as long as stderr does, wedging the whole bounded queue, unbounded during ordinary operation, recoverable only via teardown()'s 2-second shutdown watchdog. Not a regression this round introduced -- spdlog's own default error handler has the identical same-thread-blocking property, and this is a pre-existing characteristic of spdlog's async architecture, not something #4666 created. Independently found by unhappy-path, sre, and cpp-safety, all landing MEDIUM (not HIGH: no attacker reachability, doesn't affect agent command/policy dispatch, requires two independently rare conditions to coincide, and the underlying risk shape is already disclosed to operators via unchanged server-admin.md prose). Comment rewritten to state plainly what is and isn't closed; the actual fix (move the emit off the worker thread's own critical path -- a detached best-effort emitter or non-blocking write with drop-on-EAGAIN) is named but deliberately NOT attempted this round -- tracked as an open follow-up.
